title: Prefetcher misprediction and kernel-swap investigation (SLO spike)
summary: Investigation of a short p99 latency spike on 2026-07-11 that affected a single large customer (VelaChat). The spike was isolated to a 2-3 minute window where p99 jumped to ~1.6s. Initial hypotheses included memory pressure and batching regressions; subsequent profiling pointed to repeated kernel-selection and memcpy activity triggered by the prefetcher under mixed short+long prompt traffic.
impact: Affected SLO: p99 < 1.0s violated for ~2.5 minutes. No increase in error rate. Throughput kept steady. Customer-visible slowdown for VelaChat during their morning surge.
timeline:
2026-07-11T09:12Z - Alert from Console p99 dashboard.
2026-07-11T09:13Z - CS reports degradation from VelaChat.
2026-07-11T09:14Z - On-call collected NVTX traces and runtime logs.
2026-07-11T09:16Z - Temporary mitigation: reduce prefetcher concurrency on route.
2026-07-11T09:20Z - p99 returned to baseline.
2026-07-11 to 2026-07-14 - offline analysis and profiling.
2026-07-18 - Hotfix PR opened.
2026-07-19 - Canary rollout.
2026-07-20 - Broad rollout to prod.
root_cause: A combination of prefetcher misprediction and kernel-selection heuristics. Burst of short prompts interspersed with occasional ~2k-token requests caused the prefetcher to aggressively issue GPU prefetch work. Concurrently, kernel-selection decided to switch to an alternate fused kernel for some long-context requests. The interaction caused rapid kernel churn: cancelled small kernels, memcpy spikes as the alternate kernel was prepared, and a transient serialization on a global GPU coordination mutex in the runtime. The result was amplified tail latency without affecting p95 or error rates.
evidence: NVTX timelines from canary traces showing frequent small kernel launches interrupted by short memcpy spikes
nvprof flamegraph with high time in kernel-selection and kernel-launch callpaths during spike window
Device counters: sm_efficiency drop (~12%), memcpy_bandwidth up 3x on affected GPU
Runtime events: correlated 'kernel_swap_triggered' log entries for requests crossing 1024-token boundary
Heap and allocation logs show no OOMs and memory usage within expected headroom
mitigation_and_hotfix:
Short term: route-level prefetcher concurrency throttle and emergency backoff for kernel_swap events reduced the tail within minutes.
Hotfix PR: adjust prefetcher heuristic to consider recent kernel_swap rate, implement a kernel pin guard to avoid launching alternate kernels while a swap is in-flight, and add a soft serialization window to batch prefetch launches. Added NVTX markers for kernel-selection for better observability.
